Posted February 27, 2003
Analysis By Richard Cowan

As I watch the seemingly inexhaustible torrent of prohibitionist propaganda I am reminded of the Greek myth about Hercules and the stables of King Augeas.

The term Augean stables means a huge mess, because King Augeas had a vast number of cattle, which were herded into the stables every night, but no one cleaned up after them. (Governments always expect other people to do their dirty work.)

As a consequence, the stables overflowed with what the Greeks called drug education.
See
The Prohibitionist Internet Strategy:
www.we-can-lie-louder-than-you-can-tell-the-truth.con
Analysis By Richard Cowan

As in Hercules time, the government provides the fodder at one end, and the other end the Greeks called it the media produce the desired product.

It stank to high heaven, but it seemed impossible to do anything about it.

Most people said it was beneath their dignity even to think about it, although that did not stop them from writing about it. They said that the only reason that it stank was because some people complained about the smell. If everyone who lived near the stables would just stop breathing, it wouldn't be a problem.

However, as part of a plea bargain, Hercules was given the task of cleaning the stables, but he had to do it all in only one day. Clearly not even he could shovel that fast, and I know just how he must have felt.

Being a superhero, Hercules managed the feat, and the way he did it gives me hope. He diverted a couple of rivers to flow through the stables and flushed them out.

Meanwhile back in the real world, what does this have to do with the war on us? What are the rivers that we can divert?

One clue actually comes from the myth. When King Augeas refused to pay Hercules, as he had promised he would, the king's son told the truth, and was exiled for doing so. (He was sent to a place the Greeks called DEAland, which he said reminded him of his father's stables.)

In fact, young people are getting fed up with the lies that are being told to them  supposedly to protect them.
See
How the War On Marijuana To Save The Children
Has Become A War On the Children To Save Marijuana Prohibition

College newspapers are running editorials attacking the prohibitionist propaganda campaign. At the last NORML conference, everyone was very encouraged by the intelligence and drive demonstrated by the students who were there. There are more and more NORML chapters on campuses, and the Students for a Sensible Drug Policy is now on dozens of campuses.

The next point of leverage from there should be the journalism schools. Any journalism school that isn't teaching its students to question the most omnipresent government propaganda, is not teaching journalism but trade journal writing, and journalism students are being cheated.
See
We Have Reality Entertainment, So What About Some Reality News? Public Distrust And The Reality/Media Credibility Gap.
and
How Marijuana Prohibition Corrupts All Of Our Institutions
 Medicine, Law Enforcement, Journalism
And How That Corruption Sustains Prohibitionism


There is another group that is finally showing signs of awareness, religious leaders.
See
Religious Leaders Finally Beginning To Organize Opposition To The Drug War, A Mutiny for Mercy, But For Christians There May Be A More Compelling Reason Than They Realize.

It is not a matter of politics, but of morality that they must address. The churches have played a key role in the anti-slavery and civil rights movements. They cannot remain silent any longer about the war on the young and the old.
See
The Theory and Practice of Chaos Analysis By Richard Cowan

Finally, it should be obvious that the Internet is the key to all of this. It is clear that the conventional media have failed the people, so the answer is that we must become the media.

While we have a new technology, this is very similar to the Samizdat self-publication in the Soviet Union. It also happened 500 years ago when the printing press circumvented the Church's control over The Book. However, the immediacy of the Internet makes it more than just a means of communication, it is a community.
See
Australia, New Zealand, Sweden, The International Prohibitionist Counterattack,
and How We Can Use The Internet
and
An Interview With Gary Webb Shows The Importance of The Internet And The Alternative Press
and
The Internet Is Our Weapon:
Anti-Prohibitionists " lack the power of the prohibitionists, but make up for it in scholarship. "

What I am describing here is a strategy based on the assumption that we, the anti-prohibitionist movement, cannot shovel our way out of the Augean Stables of prohibition. We must divert the attention of other powerful forces in our society to address something that is as much their problem as it is ours.

At the very least, we must recognize that no mythical hero is going to do it for us, and remember something else that the Greeks said that was definitely not a myth:

Eternal vigilance is the price of liberty.
